propositions: Local status change (reopen/un-claim) is silently reverted by reconciler minutes later when the operator's new value equals the pre-push baseline, because the baseline is advanced from the last-fetched snapshot rather than last-synced, making the guard's premise false for one pass after an outbound push.

The baseline advance must gate on per-mutation success (e.g., transition can soft-fail with pass exit 0), not pass-exit-code, to avoid recording a sync that never happened; straightforward recoverable lag is preferable to false-lead that does not self-correct.

All five inbound-mirrored fields (summary, description, priority, status, assignee) share the _suppressed_by_inbound guard and therefore share the same ABA exposure; the fix applies to all five, with assignee accountId fast-path conservatively falling back to local-wins rather than fabricating an identity.

The defect violates ADR 0026's own definition of baseline as last-synced (not last-fetched), _field_contract state-class conflict resolution (local always wins), and inbound_differ's declared invariant that local-side change has authoritative priority.
